You are a molecular design agent.
You may ONLY modify molecules using tools.
Only make one modification at a time.
Read the parameter descriptions for the tools very carefully.
Always ensure that your modifications don't break valence rules and do not result in a fragmented molecule.
After each successful tool call, check its result message and the updated atom table against what you intended - if it modified the wrong part of the molecule, call undo_last_change before continuing.
Every tool except crossover_molecules acts ONLY on your current working molecule (ligand 1) - none of them can see or touch the second candidate ligand. Treat ligand 2 as inspiration only: if you want to bring in one of its features, either call crossover_molecules to combine the two, or rebuild that feature yourself on your current working molecule (e.g. with add_substructure). An atom index you give to any tool other than crossover_molecules is always interpreted against your current working molecule, never against ligand 2 - do not reason about 'modifying ligand 2' and then call one of these tools, since the edit will land on the wrong molecule and likely do nothing you intended.

Ligand 1 has neither a terminal methyl nor a pendant saturated ring, so the one-call rebuild is not available here and this will take two cuts. What it does have is a usable skeleton: an anilide at atoms 1 and 18 joining a glycine sulfonamide arm to a 4-fluoroaniline. Step one discards the arm. Atom 1 is the amide carbonyl and atom 2 the methylene, a non-ring bond, so cutting there removes the CH2, the sulfonamide nitrogen, the sulfonyl and the whole chloro-trifluoromethylphenyl - seventeen atoms - and I attach a cyclopropyl to the carbonyl in their place. That leaves the cyclopropanecarboxamide of 4-fluoroaniline, which is the right cap on the wrong aniline; the second step will replace that ring with the meta-substituted one carrying the azine. Two cuts is the cost of a host with no convenient anchor, which is worth remembering when planning a generation-1 rebuild.

Atom 2 is the anilide nitrogen and atom 3 the ipso carbon of the fluorophenyl, a non-ring bond - and an aliphatic amide nitrogen is a usable anchor, which I confirmed in the last run. Cutting there discards the para-fluoroaniline, which is doubly wrong for this series: the substituents are para where meta is worth about +0.09, and a fluorine on that central ring measured as a small negative. In its place I attach the meta-substituted benzene carrying an azine with an ethynyl at C4. Ethynyl is the control the C4 scan needs: it is strongly electron-withdrawing and linear like the nitrile, but it has no heteroatom at all, so it adds no hydrogen-bond acceptor and no polar surface. If the nitrile's 0.58 is about withdrawal and shape, ethynyl should match it; if it is about the nitrogen lone pair, ethynyl should fall away. It is also the lightest of the good C4 candidates at about 277 Da, so unlike iodine or trifluoromethyl it could actually win on Phi rather than only inform.
